title: Sabarimala: every pilgrim is swami
hookLine: on the climb to Sabarimala, every stranger on the path is called swami
carry: tat tvam asi: every pilgrim carries the god's name
tomorrow: a boy walks out of his village and keeps walking. what is he looking for?

lines: A FOREST PATH UP A HILL
cards: Swami. A man in a black dhoti says it to the tea seller at the bottom of the hill. The tea seller says it back.
A pilgrim with gray hair says it to a teenager who's stopped to catch his breath, and the teenager says it to him.
On the forest path up to Sabarimala, it's how people greet each other, thank each other, ask each other to move aside. Swami: the word for a master, a holy one, the Lord, used for everyone.
Today, the pilgrimage up Ayyappa's hill.

teach.b: Tradition says that when Manikandan's work on earth was done, he shot an arrow and asked that his temple be built where it fell.
It fell on a hill in the forest: Sabarimala, where Ayyappa is worshiped seated in meditation. Pilgrims don't just set out.
For a season before the climb they keep a vow. They wear a bead necklace, dress in black or dark blue, eat simple food, give up alcohol, keep celibacy, and often walk barefoot.
From the day the necklace goes on, the pilgrim is called swami, and even Ayyappa, by name.
Each pilgrim climbs with the irumudi on the head, a cloth bundle tied in two parts: one carries offerings, including a coconut filled with ghee for the god; the other, food for the road.

The forest echoes with a chant: Swamiye saranam Ayyappa, Lord, you are my refuge, Ayyappa. On the way, pilgrims stop at Erumeli, where Ayyappa's companion in the stories, a Muslim named Vavar, is honored too.
Rich and poor wear the same dark cloth and answer to the same name.
Tradition says that above the shrine are the words tat tvam asi, that thou art, from the Upanishads. Here's the teaching.

In the Upanishads, it means the self in you, the atman, is one with Brahman, the divine in everything. The pilgrimage acts it out. If the god lives in every pilgrim, the right word for the stranger beside you is swami.

how: Pilgrims to Sabarimala keep a season of vows, wearing a bead necklace and dark clothes and calling one another swami, then climb the hill carrying the irumudi bundle on their heads, chanting Swamiye saranam Ayyappa.

games.q: what does “kerala's onam and ayyappa” mean?
o: a king crowned again, and a hill climbed once in a lifetime
a king sent away, and a hill that only priests may climb
a king welcomed home, and a hill where every pilgrim is swami

games.q: you're climbing to Sabarimala in your dark clothes, the irumudi on your head. an old pilgrim stops beside you, out of breath. what do you call him?
games.why: on the path, everyone is swami: the old man, the teenager, the tea seller. tat tvam asi: the divine you came to see is in each of them.

practice: Breathe in slowly, and on each out-breath take one step up a forest hill in your mind. Each time a face comes to mind, someone easy or someone hard, greet them inwardly the pilgrim's way: swami.
If you pray, you can say the pilgrims' chant, Swamiye saranam Ayyappa, softly, in time with the steps.

wordCard.voice: Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa. Today, the pilgrimage to Sabarimala: the vow, the two-part bundle, the chant, and every pilgrim called swami. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: 'that thou art', from the Chandogya Upanishad; tradition says the words stand above Ayyappa's shrine.

carryVoice: Your line: tat tvam asi, every pilgrim carries the god's name. A hill where every stranger is swami. Kerala, complete.
